meta.name: Better Skills — better-skills.dev
meta.description: Developer-tool marketing site with a blueprint-schematic aesthetic: hairline engineering grid, dot-matrix pixel display type, and a strict white + near-black + single amber palette. Built with Next.js + Tailwind/shadcn tokens; Geist font family with five custom GeistPixel dot-matrix variants.
source_references: https://better-skills.dev/ (browsed live 2026-08-02, 1440px + 390px viewports — single-page marketing site with 8 numbered sections: Hero, How It Works, Features, What Is A Skill, The Problem, How We Solve It, Developer Experience, Pricing, Get Started)
CSS chunks /_next/static/chunks/*.css (design tokens, GeistPixel @font-face, keyframes) and live computed styles
meta.generation_note: The site is a light-only single page (html class forced 'light'; full dark theme tokens exist in CSS but are unused on the landing). The signature is the combination of three systems: (1) a blueprint 'drawing sheet' frame — full-width hairline divider bars marked [ 01 / 08 ] · SECTION-NAME with crosshair registration squares at grid intersections; (2) dot-matrix display type (custom GeistPixel fonts) where the amber-highlighted clause of every heading carries the emphasis; (3) scattered pixel-square confetti that flickers via a steps() CSS animation. Everything else is deliberately flat: no shadows, no gradients, no canvas/WebGL.

color.palette_type: monochromatic neutral (white/near-black) + single amber accent — custom amber scale, not Tailwind defaults

primary.role: amber-500; CTAs, heading accent words, icons, check marks, numbers, active states

secondary.role: secondary surface (zinc-100); rarely used on the mostly-white page

accent.role: same amber doubles as accent; amber-300 #FFD236 for lighter pixel glyphs, amber-600 #DD7400 / amber-700 #B75000 for deeper shades, amber-950 #461901 as text on amber buttons

neutral.usage: white page; #E5E5E5 hairline borders and blueprint grid lines; #737373 secondary/body-muted text; #A1A1A1 faint labels and pixel-square confetti gray; #0A0A0A headings and primary text

semantic.success: amber check glyphs stand in for success in feature lists (no green observed)

surface.elevated: #FFFFFF — elevation communicated by borders, not shadow or tint

color.dark_tokens_exist_but_unused: full .dark scale shipped (bg #0A0A0A, card #171717, border #2F2F2F, muted-fg #A1A1A1, amber primary unchanged); landing forces light
color.contrast_strategy: near-black on white for structure and headings; #737373 gray for supporting copy; amber reserved strictly for emphasis — accent words in headings, CTAs, icons, ordinal numbers — never for large fills or backgrounds beyond buttons and pixel glyphs

display.font: mixed — black clause in GeistPixelLine, amber clause in GeistPixelSquare; letter 'o' in hero replaced by hexagon logo glyph ('Sec⬡nd Brain')

heading_2.font: GeistPixelSquare for all section h2s; accent clause colored amber

heading_3.font: Geist (sans) for card titles, with the key word switched to amber GeistPixelSquare

body_small.font: Geist, #737373 — card body copy and sub-headlines

caption.font: Geist Mono uppercase — eyebrows '// SECTION \\', card labels ('TERMINAL', 'SECOND BRAIN'), panel headers

overline.font: Geist Mono — section sheet markers '[ 01 / 08 ] · HOW IT WORKS' with amber ordinal and small amber caret block; corner tags '[ SKILL ] [ SYNC ] [ .MD ] [ GRAPH ]'

font_families.heading: GeistPixelSquare / GeistPixelLine (custom dot-matrix variants of Geist Mono, woff2, weight 500) — five variants shipped: Square, Grid, Circle, Triangle, Line; fallback Geist Mono → ui-monospace stack
font_families.mono: Geist Mono (variable) for code, labels, markers; Fira Mono (400/500) also loaded for select mono text (pricing feature lists)

typography.font_style_notes: Three-voice system: dot-matrix pixel type for display headings (retro LED/printer feel), clean geometric-hygienic Geist for product copy, Geist Mono for engineering annotations. Headings mix voices inline: Geist sans/pixel black clause + amber pixel clause. Product UI (login) drops pixel type entirely for bold Geist.

spacing.scale: Tailwind default 0.25rem steps; sections padded generously (~120-160px vertical rhythm)
spacing.content_density: spacious — large empty regions around a narrow centered column; cards airy with ~32px padding
spacing.section_rhythm: each of the 8 sections is a 'drawing sheet': full-width hairline divider bar with sheet marker '[ NN / 08 ] · NAME', then a wide quiet band containing eyebrow + heading + sub + content; alternating tall content sections and near-empty breathing bands

layout.grid_system: centered single column inside a full-bleed blueprint grid — faint hairline verticals/horizontals with outlined-square crosshairs at intersections spanning the whole viewport
layout.max_content_width: ~1152px centered content column; hero ~90vh; login card ~530px
layout.columns: 3-col card grids (steps, problem, features 3x2), 2x2 (solve-it cards), 2-col centered pricing, 2-col split for skill-package and terminal sections (copy left, panel right)
layout.gutter: ~24-32px; feature grid uses shared hairline dividers instead of gaps
layout.breakpoints: mobile ~390px: nav collapses to wordmark + Sign In, hero stacks centered, grids go single column, install command truncates with ellipsis
layout.alignment_tendency: centered headings and hero; left-aligned card content; strict underlying grid with symmetric margins

border_radius.pill: not used — geometry stays rectilinear to match the pixel/blueprint language (base token .625rem exists but marketing surfaces render near-square)

shape.border_usage: ubiquitous 1px hairlines #E5E5E5 — every card, panel, divider, and the background grid itself; amber used on small border accents (badge, caret)
shape.divider_style: full-width hairline bars doubling as sheet markers, with outlined-square crosshair nodes at intersections and a small amber caret before the section ordinal; card-internal hairlines with tiny square handles

elevation.shadow_style: none — the page is deliberately flat
elevation.depth_cues: hairline borders, grid layering, and tonal steps (white / #FAFAFA / gray text) only; overlapping pixel squares provide the only sense of layering

iconography.style: small amber stroke glyphs (globe, terminal, sync arrows, shield) + folder/file icons in the vault tree (amber file glyph for SKILL.md) + pixel-art mosaics (amber/gray square clusters, incl. a pixel robot) as illustration; hexagon logo mark; amber checks in lists
iconography.preferred_set: custom inline SVG (115 SVGs on the page); agent logos (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, Gemini) as brand tiles in the terminal section

motion.easing: linear/steps for ambient pixel flicker; standard ease-out for reveals
motion.entrance_pattern: IntersectionObserver/useInView-triggered fade + slight translate as sections enter the viewport (content is hidden until scrolled into view; CSS 'enter/exit' keyframes)
motion.exit_pattern: none observed — once revealed, content stays
motion.philosophy: minimal functional + ambient texture: one quiet trick (flickering pixel cells via steps(3) opacity keyframes) instead of showy animation; no WebGL, no scroll-scrubbing, no parallax

components.button_style: primary: #F99C00 amber fill, #461901 dark-brown label, ~2-4px radius, arrow → suffix ('Get Started →'); secondary: white fill, 1px #E5E5E5 border, black label ('See on GitHub'); login OAuth buttons: full-width white bordered rows with brand icon
components.input_style: install-command bar: 1px bordered white box, Geist Mono text, amber '$' prompt, trailing copy icon button; truncated with ellipsis on mobile
components.card_style: white, 1px hairline border, ~4px radius, flat; header zone with pixel-art mosaic or amber icon + uppercase mono label, Geist semibold title with amber pixel-font keyword, gray 14-15px body; amber mono ordinal (01-04) top-right on step/solve cards
components.navigation_pattern: top white bar: hexagon logo + 'BETTER-SKILLS.' Geist Mono wordmark left, centered Geist gray links (Features/Pricing/Docs/GitHub), amber Sign In button right; no dropdowns; mobile collapses to wordmark + button
components.list_style: pricing features: amber ✓ + Fira Mono 14px items separated by hairlines; vault explorer: indented file tree with folder icons and mono filenames
components.component_notes: badge: bordered chip with amber ✦ + 'Open source'; section eyebrows as '// NAME \\' mono; sheet-marker divider bars; skill-graph panel = bordered frame with '// SKILL GRAPH' + '11 SKILLS' mono header and an SVG node-link diagram (amber primary nodes, gray secondary nodes, mono labels); terminal panel with square window-dots and 'TERMINAL' header; footer = wordmark + 3 mono-caps link columns + bottom hairline with © 2026 BETTER-SKILLS, Inc.

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: an engineering blueprint / EDA drawing sheet crossed with a dot-matrix LED board — registration crosshairs, sheet numbers [ 01 / 08 ], mono annotations, and pixel typography
aesthetic.era_influence: 1980s CAD/blueprint drafting + dot-matrix print/LED signage, executed with 2020s Vercel-style restraint (Geist, flat, hairlines)

visual_language.complexity: minimal-to-moderate — few elements per viewport, each heavily stylized
visual_language.ornamentation: subtle accents: pixel-square confetti, crosshair registration marks, mono brackets, hexagon glyph — ornaments are systematic, never decorative flourishes
visual_language.whitespace_usage: abundant — entire sections are mostly empty grid; whitespace is the dominant material
visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: weight concentrated in the centered heading + one content cluster per section; edges stay empty grid
visual_language.focal_strategy: single focal point per viewport — the dot-matrix heading with its amber clause
visual_language.contrast_level: high type contrast (near-black on white) but low element contrast (hairlines, gray text); amber acts as the single high-chroma signal
visual_language.texture_usage: blueprint hairline grid + flickering pixel cells as the only texture

composition.hierarchy_method: typographic hierarchy + color: dot-matrix scale for sections, amber to mark the operative word; sheet markers pace the scroll like numbered drawing sheets
composition.balance_type: symmetric around a centered axis, with asymmetric split panels (copy left / artifact right) inside sections
composition.flow_direction: strict vertical chapter flow (01→08), each chapter announced by its divider bar
composition.grouping_strategy: hairline-bounded cards and panels; shared-divider grids for feature sets
composition.negative_space_role: structural — empty grid bands separate chapters and make the annotations readable

imagery.illustration_style: pixel-art mosaics built from amber + gray squares (incl. a pixel robot for 'Agent'), SVG node-link skill graph, file-tree and terminal UI vignettes
imagery.graphic_elements: crosshair squares, bracketed mono tags '[ SKILL ]', amber caret blocks, hexagon logo, agent brand tiles
imagery.pattern_usage: blueprint grid as global background pattern; pixel confetti clusters at section corners
imagery.image_shape: squares and rectilinear panels only — no circles, blobs, or organic shapes (except graph nodes)

interaction_feel.feedback_style: quiet — standard hover states; copy affordance on the install command
interaction_feel.hover_behavior: subtle color/darken shifts on buttons and links
interaction_feel.transition_personality: fade-subtle with gentle rise on scroll
interaction_feel.microinteraction_density: low — the ambient pixel flicker is the only persistent motion

brand_voice_in_ui.tone: assured, developer-fluent, economy of words ('Define once. Reuse as a skill.', 'Install once. Stay in sync.')
brand_voice_in_ui.formality: casual-professional; sentence-case headings, no exclamation except community line
brand_voice_in_ui.cta_style: direct imperative with arrow suffix ('Get Started →', 'Talk to Founders')

overview.effect_intensity: subtle-accent — ambient pixel flicker + scroll reveals; nothing immersive
overview.performance_tier: lightweight — CSS keyframes + SVG + IntersectionObserver; zero canvas elements, no WebGL context, no GSAP/Three/Lenis/framer-motion detected
overview.fallback_strategy: graceful by construction — effects are pure CSS/SVG; content readable with animations disabled
overview.primary_technology: CSS keyframes (ascii-flicker, enter/exit, ping-sequence, pulse, rotate-sequence) + inline SVG + IntersectionObserver/useInView reveals

background_effects.description: global hairline blueprint grid with outlined-square crosshairs at intersections; scattered amber/gray pixel-square clusters whose cells flicker opacity via steps(3) keyframes
background_effects.technology: CSS backgrounds/SVG + 'ascii-flicker' keyframes (opacity oscillates ~0.02→0.06, steps(3,end), infinite)

params.density: sparse clusters at hero edges and section corners

particle_systems.description: pixel squares are static-position cells with opacity flicker, not a moving particle system

text_effects.description: dot-matrix pixel typeface (GeistPixel variants) does the work of a text effect; hero mixes GeistPixelLine (black clause) + GeistPixelSquare (amber clause) and substitutes the letter 'o' with the hexagon logo image; amber keyword swap inside card titles and h2s

image_effects.description: no photographic imagery; pixel-art and logos are static

svg_animations.description: 115 inline SVGs: the skill-graph node-link diagram (amber/gray nodes, mono labels) inside a bordered panel, pixel-art mosaics, icons, and crosshair/grid ornaments; ambient sequences via CSS keyframes (ping-sequence, rotate-sequence) rather than SMIL

visual_effects.composite_notes: The entire effects budget goes into one coherent illusion: the page is a drafting sheet that is faintly alive. The hairline grid, sheet-number dividers, and crosshairs are static; the pixel cells flicker with a stepped opacity animation (ascii-flicker), which reads as electronic rather than organic. Dot-matrix type carries the retro-electronics theme so no additional text animation is needed. Everything is CSS/SVG — no runtime graphics libraries — keeping the page fast and the aesthetic crisp at any DPI.
